extracted.intended_audience: The Higher and Middle Classes (explicit audience in the sermon)
extracted.subtask_description: A sermon-style guide for members of the higher and middle classes to recognise, analyse, and oppose demagogues and political mountebanks — describing who they are, their qualifications/conduct, their tactics, causes of public distress, and suitable remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-question framework for examining the public case
rubrics_metrics.description: The whole remaining subject may be comprised in the three questions implied ... First, who are they who have hitherto prescribed for the case, and are still tampering with it? What are their qualifications? What has been their conduct? Second, what is the true seat and source of the complaint — the ultimate causes as well as the immediate occasions? And lastly, what are the appropriate medicines? Who and where are the true physicians?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these three questions as the organising rubric when assessing public complaints and proposed remedies: identify the actors (their character and record), diagnose root and proximate causes, and assess remedies (who is fit to administer them). The sermon treats each question in sequence as the method for judging political prescriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watch for the sudden elevation of worthless persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Worthless persons of little or no estimation for rank, learning, or integrity ... are suddenly cried up as men of enlarged views and liberal sentiments, our only genuine patriots and philanthropists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be suspicious when persons of dubious private character are loudly proclaimed public benefactors; cross-check personal integrity, learning, and prior conduct rather than trusting crowd acclaim or novelty of appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demagogue's hypocrisy (practice of hypocrisy)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the main characteristics of demagogues in all ages is, to practise hypocrisy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hypocrisy manifests as public professions of patriotism or pity that mask private vice or self-interest. Test for consistency between public advocacy and private behaviour, and beware of those who denounce the faults they themselves practise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passion for vague and violent invective
rubrics_metrics.description: A passion for vague and violent invective, an habitual and inveterate predilection for the language of hate and rage and contumely, an ungoverned appetite for abuse and defamation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify speakers who routinely rely on denunciation, abuse, or contempt rather than reasoned argument. Such invective is an indicator of demagogic intent and poor grounds for trustworthy public prescriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heart works iniquity — planning and executing evil
rubrics_metrics.description: His heart will work iniquity. That is, he will plan evil, and do his utmost to carry his plans into execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish mere harsh rhetoric from systematic designs to harm or profit by public disturbance; assess whether a speaker's aims are to produce beneficial reform or to pursue destructive/private ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: They utter error against the Lord / make empty the soul of the needy
rubrics_metrics.description: Not alone to utter error, but to utter error against the Lord, to make empty the soul of the needy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware political rhetoric that corrupts moral teaching or misleads the needy into actions contrary to their real interests. Test claims by their real effects on the poor, not by rhetorical appeals to their grievances.

rubrics_metrics.name: They plead for the poor but actually plead against them
rubrics_metrics.description: They plead to the poor and ignorant — nowhere and at no time are they found actually pleading for them. Nor is this the worst. They even plead against them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scrutinise allegedly pro-poor proposals for hidden effects that worsen the poor's situation (e.g., fomenting unrest that reduces actual relief). Evaluate policies by outcomes, not rhetorical solidarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument: bold, warm, and earnest assertions regardless of facts
rubrics_metrics.description: 1. Bold, warm, and earnest assertions, it matters not whether supported by facts or no, nay, though they should involve absurdities, and demonstrable impossibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat confident, emotive assertions with skepticism when unsupported by facts; rhetorical fervour can substitute for evidence. Demand factual grounding and check for demonstrable absurdities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument: startling particular facts divorced from context
rubrics_metrics.description: 2. Startling particular facts, which, discovered from their context, enable a man to convey falsehood while he says truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware of isolated, sensational facts presented without context; verify the broader context and whether the particular instance legitimately supports the general claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument: argument from passing events / appeal to immediacy
rubrics_metrics.description: 3. Arguments built at passing events, and deriving an undue importance from the feelings of the moment. The mere appeal ... to the audience whether the arguments are not such that none but an idiot or a hireling could resist, is an effective substitute for any argument at all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious of reasoning that exploits current passions or temporary incidents to draw sweeping conclusions; require longitudinal or structural evidence rather than emotional immediacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument: display defects without accompanying advantages
rubrics_metrics.description: 4. The display of defects without the accompanying advantages, or vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess both costs and benefits; rhetoric that emphasizes disadvantages while concealing compensating advantages (or the reverse) is manipulative. Demand a balanced account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument: conceal the general/ultimate result behind local scenery
rubrics_metrics.description: 5. Concealment of the general and ultimate result behind the scenery of local and particular consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probe whether presented local anecdotes mask general consequences. Ask for an explicit account of long-term and system-wide effects rather than relying on evocative particulars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument: true-only-under-conditions statements presented as general truths
rubrics_metrics.description: 6. Statement of positions that are true only under particular conditions, to men whose ignorance or fury make them forget that these conditions are not present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the conditionality of claims. Warning: many propositions apply only under narrow assumptions; exposing absent conditions neutralises false generalisations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument: chains of questions & technical objections
rubrics_metrics.description: 7. Chains of questions — especially of such questions as the persons best authorized to propose are ever the slowest in proposing; and objections intelligible of themselves, the answers to which require the comprehension of a system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise the tactic of posing many leading or technical questions to confuse lay audiences; require clear, system-level exposition and avoid being baited by complexity designed to intimidate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument: vague/commonplace satire mixed with recent anecdote
rubrics_metrics.description: 8. Vague and commonplace satire, stale as the wine in which flies were drowned last summer, seasoned by the sly tale and important anecdote of but yesterday, that came within the speaker's own knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify use of trite satire plus a recent, 'inside' anecdote to produce apparent originality; resist being persuaded by novelty that lacks substantive argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument: transitions from audacious charge to flattering interpretative lies
rubrics_metrics.description: 9. Transitions from the audacious charge ... to the lie pregnant and interpretative; the former to prove the orator's courage ... the latter to flatter the sagacity of the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch for rhetorical moves that shift from shocking accusation (to display bravery) to plausible-sounding reinterpretations (to flatter listeners). These switches are strategic rather than evidentiary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument: jerks of style — alternating lunatic trope and buffoonery
rubrics_metrics.description: 10. Jerks of style, from the lunatic trope ... to the buffoonery and 'red-lattice phrases' ... the one in ostentation of superior rank and the other in pledge of heartiness and good fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note abrupt stylistic shifts meant to signal elitism or camaraderie in turn; such theatricality is used to manipulate different audience emotions rather than to present sober argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument: leave impression of imminent great change and rely on passions
rubrics_metrics.description: 11. Lasty, and throughout all, to leave a general impression of something striking, something that is to come of it, and to rely on the indolence of men's understandings and the activity of their passions for their resting in this state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be alert to rhetoric that promises dramatic future outcomes without substantive causal mechanism; demand concrete plans and evidence rather than vague promises.

rubrics_metrics.name: They 'bend their tongues as a bow' — use deceit as weapon
rubrics_metrics.description: "They bend their tongues as a bow! they shoot out deceits as arrows: they are prophets of the deceit of their own hearts: they cause the people to err by their dreams and their lightness: they make the people vain, they feed them with wormwood, they give them the water of gall for drink: and the people love to have it so." (Jeremiah cited)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summative criterion: demagogues weaponize deceit and illusions to inflame vanity and appetite for false consolations. Evaluate rhetoric by whether it aims to enlighten or to inflame, and whether follow-through harms the people it claims to help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demagogues are enemies of liberty of the press and of education
rubrics_metrics.description: If they are the enemies of liberty in general ... still more emphatically are they the enemies of the liberty of the PRESS in particular; and therein of all the truths, human and divine, which a free press is the most efficient and only commensurate means of protecting, extending, and perpetuating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take hostility to free press or education as a red flag: those who denounce access to education or freedom of the press are likely undermining safeguards against their own mendacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slander & sophistry to chill charitable action
rubrics_metrics.description: If they cannot dissuade the liberal from devising liberal things, they will at least blacken the motives of his beneficence. If they cannot close the hand of the giver, they will at least embitter the gift in the mouth of the receivers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify tactics that aim to poison public gratitude or discredit charitable efforts via motive-attack and slander. Test proposals by likely effects on mutual trust and the reception of relief by beneficiaries.
